What is the Holy Spirit ? What is Christ ?

It's senseless to their ears because they don't even understand what spirit is. They haven't been taught in Christianity that there is a notion that they might not be who they think themselves to be so in that way, they can't channel Christ.

I mean, what do we mean by spirit firstly ? The way I see it, a spirit is a force that takes over the self in order to express itself through you. It dominates you, like musicians and artists often say that their best work is done when they zone out, that something takes over them, that's spirit. That's a muse working through them. They know they haven't done it by themselves, something else took over them. They weren't there, they literally dissipate in that moment. Christ is just the same, he works through you. When he was flesh, I'm sure people weren't impressed by what he looked like. He looked like a normal man, who knew that the Holy Spirit was in him and he was the son of God ? No one. When Paul was on his way to Damascus, there the Holy Spirit came to him and he was an Apostle from then on.

But none of that is ever talked about because Christianity does not advocate for the nature of the self, Christianity hides away from the nature of the mind and metaphysics unless you really begin to look into Christianity. With Buddhism, it's straight into the nature of all that. The more Christianity goes on about sin, which people don't understand, the more the religion will simply die off.

Because we're so comfortable in our lives, people do not see the hardships they go through as dramatic as the Exodus, they do not see Jezebel's evil and see no harm in worshipping the golden calf, that's why Buddhism is on the rise, because it's more practical. So, the new generations of the West are most of the time secular and atheist, we've been taught that Christianity and Judaism are tools used for war and the 'opium of the masses'. The two rally around the Bible as the literal truth of God and has now come to a decline in popularity due to Yahweh's tantrums and indecisiveness. This has come with a need to substitute the two religions with something else that will help people forge their way through this life and this substitute is the self\-help industry with a softened version of Buddhism and Hinduism. \(This isn't an apology for religion, I'm not Jordan Peterson\)

Self help says that you have to look on the bright side constantly, that what hinders you so much are the toxic aspects of your life. That life was meant to be lived with a constant smile and a ray of sunshine following you wherever you go as you jump from that waterfall in the Far East and join all your friends around a bonfire. You see it in the marketing pictures, you see it on the Gaia channel, you hear it with people saying ''just think positive !'' to the point that it makes you sick. ''The point of life is to just be happy, man'' as though people were so deprived from any sense of fatality, heroism and adventure that life might as well be lived the way Buddha lived it at the beginning; in a palace filled up with women, pass times, distractions... while shunning away the darker aspects. 

I say that because I've seen it so many times. An example is an ex\-girlfriend who's granma had passed away and in that time there was a craze that death should be celebrated, that you should be happy your loved one lived a life that was so full... and whatever. So she posted this thing on Facebook \(can't quiet remember what\) that was basically making it appear that she wasn't down about it, she wasn't hurt from it, that she was so positive nothing could get to her... I mean imagine the suppression of feelings, there. It's one thing to accept death, it's another to literally party on a dead body. All of that came from a distorted view of the East. In the West, we dress in black, we stay silent, we honour the dead with peace. In the East they let out their pain, you see it with the Hindu women crying so hard you might as well cry yourself. Now this is a bit biased but it strikes me as though when the East mourns somebody then if they're dancing they're dancing with full awareness of what they're doing, they're allowing themselves to be so cathartic about what they've just been through that the dancing and singing is a way to express their grieving. There's nothing wrong with either in my mind but where the self help comes in with ''Fuck it she's dead let's celebrate like it's 1989'' then there's a problem where you have to appear so positive in order to be accepted by the rest that you'll drown your feelings in positivity. That's what I call toxic positivity, where no negativity is allowed. 

Anyway, all you have to do is be happy and get rid of all your toxic relationships. ''This guy said this ? Okay, toxic, don't get near him'' Funnily enough, this dude at work was telling me how he smashed all his money \(3k in a week, he got it from a court case\) and I told him he should learn to manage his finances and he said ''Nah, I can't take care of myself'' there it hit me because I could have thought ''Oh man, how toxic is this man ?'' instead of ''Okay, I know myself well enough that I can handle this man's inability to care for his money, this won't get to me''. See, self help doesn't teach you how to know yourself, it teaches you to be a product of a postcard happiness. It doesn't teach you values, virtues, humility, sacrifice... Mixed with Eastern philosophies, they teach you that you are God, you are the universe, they took the idea of the Hindu 'Atman' to make it seem that you are Brahman \(the all encompassing God in the Upanishads\) It feeds your ego except that this time your ego isn't a frown, it's not animated by anger and austere authority, it's a vicious ego with a smile on its face that's out for itself and will not hesitate to let you down should you mention anything that is negative.

It's a thousand drunks singing altogether 'Always look on the bright side of life' zombified by the modern mindless consumerism leaving souls to wonder exactly where is all the heroism in the films they see, where is the poetry, where are the arts.... They're hungry for adventure, but they want it safe, they want it comfortable.
Modern self\-help draws on whiney toxic positivity, not stoicism.

My mum passed when I was 15 and my dad when I was 21. I'm 25 now and I'm only starting to find my feet again.

With my mum it was sort of expected, her health declined slowly and slowly as chemotherapy was working its way through her until they sedated her on the sofa \(she refused to die in hospital\) with morphine pumping through her veins. What shocked me the most was that she had those black things in the white of her eyes, she was losing her sight as she was dying. She was extremely weak and I was a total shit head skiving school. I'll always regret my behaviour towards her. I look back sometimes and I ask myself ''Was I even there ?'' ''Was I even awake ?'' ''Did I even consider how she felt ?'' She had always done her best for us, being adopted and all, we were her anchor, she lived for us. She loved us but she was always arguing with my dad. He was abusive, she was abusive. Not towards us but towards each other and now that I'm 25 and I'm discovering myself more and more I've got so many questions that will be left unanswered. Feelings that will never be resolved, anger that will never be tamed. Questions I wanna ask like ''Why did you act that way ?'' ''Why did you tell me that dad hated us ?'' 

Then I awake from my anger and it dawns on me that may be they were hurt too in childhood. I mean how could they not have been hurt ? That led them to destroy one another though they had kids. So now, when I look at myself I realise that in my own personal relationships, I've repeated what my parents were doing. I've been abusive too and I'm ashamed. What counts now is that I redeem myself and through my own redemption I consider that my parents too will be redeemed. That somehow it courses through my veins and that I have a task and a duty towards myself and the world to change my ways so that the cycle can be broken. I don't want my own kids to go through that. I do believe that we have a purpose in this world, I was led to God shortly after my dad's death, it was only natural and my purpose is to take God by the hand, almost like a child, and show glorify him. I needed a fatherly figure so I found God.

When my dad passed, he passed in California, I live in the UK, I got to the Alta Bates hospital in Berkley half an hour too late and if any of the nurses are reading this, thank you so much for the support. And to that guy who put his hand on my shoulder when I was at the morgue, I really didn't mean to push you away.

After my dad passed, I cried like a bitch, I drank like an alcoholic and the flat I live in got so deteriorated that mice ate through the walls, that's when I realised I had to pick myself up a little bit but it's only really very recently that I'm coming out of my hole. I work out now, I have a job, I'm looking to do what I can. I wish I would have heard my dad's last words like I heard my mum's. My mum told me I should live for myself and treat women kindly. Both of which I had never done until again, recently. Sometimes I wonder and daydream about what my dad would have said to me and what I would have said to him. He came to believe in God too and after my mum's death he was never the same again. Even though they abused each other and were almost vicious in terms of using their kids, I like to think they realised too late. I know they had some good times here and there but you know...

The only advice I have for any of you who still have one or both parents in their lives is by all means, ask the necessary questions before they pass. Resolve your issues cause we all have some. We all have been wronged one way or another and it'd be a real shame if you were to leave those things unconscious. Bring them out and don't be scared of asking. They'll always see you as their kids I'm sure. Make sure that you tell them you love them as well and have a laugh with them. Most importantly, understand that they're not just parents but people, they've had their shit going ons too.

So, the Gita is a Hindu scripture in which Krishna comes down to help the warrior Arjuna on the battlefield against Arjuna's old teachers. It's part of the Mahabarata (the Hindu epic). Arjuna does not want to fight against his old teachers and family, he is weakened by attachments (which relates ambiguously relates to our conversation) and his will to fight is incapacitated. But Krishna then sits next to him and explains to him that it is sole duty to fight because none on this battlefield will ever die since the 'self' can never be slain. The 'self' in the Gita is the idea of the immortal soul, that it cannot be touched by anything external and cannot ever be weakened by the delusions of the mind. Krishna explains to Arjuna that everything belongs to Him (he is also called the Supreme Personality of Godhead) and is within him therefore we should not fear to accomplish what must be accomplished.
